comment: Every case here asserts the FAIL-SAFE direction: a clause the device cannot read, cannot understand, or that says 'stop' must lock, and a DST boundary must not shift a countdown by an hour. Driven through the enforcer entry point (compute_remaining), NOT a library helper — the paused-with-no-caps hole (02-B4) survived for months precisely because every existing vector drove quota_left instead. Review 2026-09-21, findings 02-B4/B5/B6/G1/G2 and 02b-G4.

enforcer.name: paused_budget_with_no_caps_locks
enforcer.why: 02-B4: wire-paused carrying neither cap read as UNBOUNDED to the enforcer while the exported helper said zero. The contract: 'When true, blocks all time (quota = 0). Distinct from absent.'

enforcer.name: paused_budget_with_a_daily_cap_only_locks_on_both_axes
enforcer.why: 02-B4: paused is zero on both axes whichever caps the body carries, so no surface can read an unset axis as 'no limit'.

enforcer.name: future_budget_version_locks
enforcer.why: 02-G1: serde drops unknown fields, so a v:2 body that moved to dailySeconds would parse here as NO CAP. An unimplemented version is an unreadable budget.

enforcer.name: future_budget_version_outranks_revoked
enforcer.why: 02-G1: revoked is the one arm that means 'unbounded'. A body we cannot read must not reach it on the strength of a field that happens to share a v1 name.

enforcer.name: future_schedule_version_locks_malformed
enforcer.why: 02-G1: an unimplemented schedule version reads as unparseable — the same fail-SAFE a clause file we cannot read takes — never as a v1 schedule.

enforcer.name: future_schedule_version_locks_even_with_no_windows
enforcer.why: 02-G1: an empty weekly set is otherwise UNBOUNDED. The version check outranks every arm, including the one that imposes nothing.

enforcer.name: unparseable_timezone_locks_malformed
enforcer.why: 02-G2: the fail-safe arm the enforcer has always had, now actually covered by a vector.

enforcer.name: paused_schedule_locks_with_no_countdown
enforcer.why: 02-G2: a paused schedule locks indefinitely, and must not offer a 'back in …' the ward could wait out.

enforcer.name: spring_forward_window_close_counts_real_seconds
enforcer.why: 02-B5: Sun 2027-03-28 00:30 Europe/London, window 00:00-06:00. The local day is 1380 minutes, so 06:00 is 4h30m away — minute-of-day arithmetic claimed 5h30m.

enforcer.name: spring_forward_next_open_counts_real_seconds
enforcer.why: 02-B5: Sat 2027-03-27 23:00 Europe/London, daily 07:00-08:00. The next open is 7h of real time away, not the 8h a 1440-minute day implies — and this is the number the lock screen shows.

enforcer.name: fall_back_window_close_counts_real_seconds
enforcer.why: 02-B5, the other direction: Sun 2026-10-25 00:30 Europe/London, window 00:00-06:00. 01:00-01:59 is lived twice, so 06:00 is 6h30m away and the old arithmetic was an hour SHORT.

enforcer.name: fall_back_next_open_counts_real_seconds
enforcer.why: 02-B5: Sat 2026-10-24 23:00 Europe/London, daily 07:00-08:00 — 9h of real time to the next open across the 25-hour day.

enforcer.name: an_unreadable_clause_outranks_a_spent_budget_in_the_explanation
enforcer.why: 02-G2: a lock the device cannot explain must never be dressed up as a decision somebody made.

tethering.name: future_version_raw_is_blocked
tethering.why: 02b-G4: the arm that survived an unrecognised body was Raw — unfiltered upstream internet, kernel-forwarded around every on-device filter. The worst fail direction in the product.

tethering.name: future_version_filtered_is_blocked
tethering.why: 02b-G4: no v2 arm is trusted, not even the conservative one.

tethering.name: implemented_version_still_evaluates
tethering.why: The guard must not block the version this build actually implements.
